lines: +# Secrets: named, scoped sets of key/value pairs (credentials, endpoints, tokens) that `CREATE SECRET` stores and DuckDB
+# resolves by path. This module lets code of your own define a kind of secret and read, create and inspect secrets.
+# There is one data handle, `secret`: a few string properties (type, provider, name, storage, persist type), scopes, and a
+# set of keys with values of any type (nested ones included), some of which are marked as redacted. The same handle is
+# what a lookup returns, what a create callback receives and fills, and what `[[context_create_secret]]` stores. Where a
+# secret is handed to you by DuckDB it can be read-only or partly fixed; each place says so.
+# Defining a kind of secret is a secret function, built with `[[secret_function_create]]`: one provider of a secret
+# type. It declares the named parameters `CREATE SECRET` accepts and a create callback that turns them into the secret.
+# Registering the first function of a type defines the type; the function marked `[[secret_function_set_default]]` is the
+# provider `CREATE SECRET (TYPE <type>)` uses when no provider is named. A type an extension of DuckDB's defines (e.g.
+# `s3` of httpfs) is never defined here: registering a provider for it loads that extension first. After registration
+# `CREATE SECRET (TYPE <type>, PROVIDER <provider>, ...)` works like it does for the secrets DuckDB ships.
+# A secret is a key/value secret. It is stored, persisted and dropped by DuckDB like any other, and a persisted
+# one is read back as a key/value secret again. Custom secret *storages* are not part of this API.
+# Secrets are read and created through a context (`context_*`) or a connection (`connection_*`), as the secret manager
+# keeps state per transaction. A lookup returns a copy: a secret that is dropped or replaced afterwards does not change
+# the handle already returned, and changing the handle does not change the stored secret.
+# Combining a secret with a setting, e.g. "the key `region` of the secret, else the option `s3_region`", is up to the
+# caller: read the secret with this module and the option with `[[config_get_option_value]]`.
+# Registration is not transactional: a registered secret function is visible to every connection at once, is not undone
+# by a rollback, and lives for as long as the instance does.
+      A string property of a secret, next to its keys. Set with `[[secret_set_property]]` and read with
+        description: The provider the secret is created with, e.g. `config`.
+          The name of the secret. A secret created without one is named `__default_<type>`, as by `CREATE SECRET`;
+          only a secret built with `[[secret_create]]` and not named yet reads back empty.
+        description: The name of the storage the secret lives in, e.g. `memory` or `local_file`. Empty when DuckDB chooses.
+          Where the secret lives, as one of `default` (DuckDB chooses, following the secret settings), `temporary` (in
+          memory for the lifetime of the instance), `persistent` (written to disk) or `transaction` (in memory for the
+          lifetime of the current transaction, for credentials a catalog hands out with a query). Matched
+          case-insensitively; read back in lower case.
+    description: What creating a secret does when a secret of the same name already exists.
+    # The values match the first three duckdb::OnCreateConflict values
+        description: Fail, as a plain `CREATE SECRET` does.
+        description: Keep the existing secret and succeed, as `CREATE SECRET IF NOT EXISTS` does.
+        description: Replace the existing secret, as `CREATE OR REPLACE SECRET` does.
+      An owned opaque handle to a secret function being built: one provider of a secret type. Created with
+      A handle to a key/value secret. Owned when built with `[[secret_create]]` or returned by
+      `[[connection_create_secret]]`): the caller destroys it with `[[secret_destroy]]` and may change it with the setters,
+      which never affects a stored secret. Borrowed when received by a create callback, valid only for the duration of
+      the call: the `input` is read-only, describing the `CREATE SECRET` statement with its options as keys, and the
+      `output` is the secret to fill, with its properties and scope already set from the statement.
+          Borrowed, read-only secret describing the `CREATE SECRET` statement: its type, provider, name, storage, persist
+          type and scope, and the options the user gave as keys with their values, each already cast to the type its
+          Borrowed secret to fill, starting out with the type, provider, name and scope of the input and no keys. Set
+          its keys with `[[secret_set_value]]` and mark sensitive ones with `[[secret_add_redacted_key]]`; its scope can be
+          changed, its properties (type, provider, name, storage and persist type) cannot. When the callback returns without an error, the secret is stored.
+        description: The user data set via `[[secret_function_set_user_data]]`, or null if none was set.
+          Borrowed handle to the context running `CREATE SECRET`, e.g. to read files or settings the secret is
+          Borrowed error info handle to use to report errors that occur during the callback. Reporting an error fails
+          the `CREATE SECRET` and creates no secret.
+      Creates a new secret function through a factory.
+      The function starts out empty: configure it with the setters, then make it available with
+      returned handle and must destroy it with `[[secret_function_destroy]]`, also after registration.
+      The function can only be registered on the instance the factory belongs to.
+        description: "The factory to create the secret function through."
+        description: "On success, receives the newly created secret function. Owned by the caller."
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Sets the secret type the function creates secrets of, as `CREATE SECRET (TYPE ...)` and
+      The name is borrowed and copied. Matched case-insensitively. A type must be set before registration.
+        description: "The secret function to set the type of."
+        description: "The name of the secret type."
+        description: The length of `type` in bytes. `type` must be valid UTF-8, need not be null-terminated, and may be NULL only when this is 0.
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Sets the provider the function implements, as `CREATE SECRET (TYPE ..., PROVIDER <provider>)` names it. Common
+      providers are `config`, which builds the secret from the named parameters alone, and `credential_chain`, which
+      looks the values up in the environment.
+      The provider is borrowed and copied. Matched case-insensitively. A provider must be set before registration.
+        description: "The secret function to set the provider of."
+        description: The length of `provider` in bytes. `provider` must be valid UTF-8, need not be null-terminated, and may be NULL only when this is 0.
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Sets whether the function is the default provider of its type: the one `CREATE SECRET (TYPE <type>)` uses when
+      the statement names no provider. Defaults to false.
+      A type without a default provider requires every statement to name its provider. Only the function that defines
+      the type, the first one registered for it, can be the default: registering a later function of an existing type
+        description: "Whether the function is the default provider of its type."
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Declares a named parameter `CREATE SECRET` accepts for this provider, e.g. `region`.
+      A value the user gives is cast to the declared type before the create callback sees it, and a parameter the
+      function does not declare is rejected. Names are matched case-insensitively. Declaring the same name twice
+        description: "The secret function to add the parameter to."
+        description: "The name of the parameter. Borrowed and copied."
+        description: The length of `name` in bytes. `name` must be valid UTF-8, need not be null-terminated, and may be NULL only when this is 0.
+        description: "The type of the parameter. Borrowed and copied."
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Sets the create callback of the secret function, invoked for every `CREATE SECRET` that resolves to its type and
+      The callback receives the statement as a read-only secret and fills a secret with the result, see
+      `[[secret_create_callback]]`. It runs on the thread running the statement, with a transaction active. A create
+      callback must be set before registration.
+        description: "The secret function to set the callback of."
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Sets arbitrary user data on the secret function.
+      Associates an opaque pointer with the function, handed to its create callback. The opaque handle bundles the
+      pointer with an optional destructor, invoked when the data is no longer needed: once the secret function handle
+      is destroyed and, if it was registered, the instance is too.
+        description: "The secret function to set the user data of."
+        description: "Opaque handle bundling the user data pointer plus an optional destructor."
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Registers the secret function on the connection's instance, visible to every connection.
+      Registration is not transactional: it takes effect at once, also inside an explicit transaction, and a rollback
+      does not undo it. Registration requires a type, a provider and a create callback, defines the type if it is new,
+      and fails with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID` when a function for the same type and provider already exists, or when the
+      function is the default provider of a type that exists already. A type an extension of DuckDB's defines (e.g.
+      `s3` of httpfs) is not defined here: registration loads that extension, autoloading it if enabled, and fails
+      with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID` (or the autoload error) when it cannot. The secret function must have been
+      created through a factory of the same instance. The caller still owns the handle after registration and must
+      destroy it with `[[secret_function_destroy]]`, which does not affect the registered function.
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Registers the secret function on the loading extension's instance, visible to every connection. A type it
+      defines is attributed to the extension in `duckdb_secret_types()`; this does not make DuckDB load the extension
+      when a statement names the type.
+      Use this from the extension's load callback. Otherwise as `[[connection_register_secret_function]]`.
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Destroys the secret function, releasing its resources.
+      Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to prevent
+      double-destruction. Destroying the handle after registration does not affect the registered function.
+      Creates a new, empty secret through a factory, to fill in and hand to `[[context_create_secret]]`.
+      The secret starts out with no properties set, no scope and no keys. The caller owns the returned handle and must
+        description: "The factory to create the secret through."
+        description: "On success, receives the newly created secret. Owned by the caller."
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Sets a string property of the secret, see `SECRET_PROPERTY`. The type is required to create the secret; the
+      provider defaults to the default provider of the type, the name to one DuckDB chooses, the storage and persist
+      The value is borrowed and copied. An invalid persist type fails with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID`. Fails with
+      `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID` on a read-only secret and on the secret a create callback fills, whose properties are fixed
+        description: The length of `value` in bytes. `value` must be valid UTF-8, need not be null-terminated, and may be NULL only when this is 0.
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Adds a scope to the secret: a path prefix, e.g. `s3://bucket/dir`, the secret applies to. A lookup for a path
+      picks the secret whose scope is the longest prefix of the path. A secret without scope applies to every path.
+      The scope is borrowed and copied. Fails with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID` on a read-only secret.
+        description: The length of `scope` in bytes. `scope` must be valid UTF-8, need not be null-terminated, and may be NULL only when this is 0.
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Removes every scope from the secret. In a create callback this includes the ones the user gave; check
+      `[[secret_get_scope_count]]` on the output first to supply a default scope only when the user gave none. Fails
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Sets the value of a key of the secret.
+      The value is borrowed and copied and can be of any type, nested ones included; a NULL value is stored as a NULL.
+      Setting a key again replaces its value. Keys are matched case-insensitively and keep the casing given first. For
+      the options of a `CREATE SECRET` this is the value the named parameter was given. Fails with
+        description: The length of `key` in bytes. `key` must be valid UTF-8, need not be null-terminated, and may be NULL only when this is 0.
+        description: "The value to store. Borrowed and copied."
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Marks a key as sensitive, so that its value is never displayed: `duckdb_secrets()` and the echo of `CREATE
+      SECRET` show it as `redacted`, while `[[secret_get_value]]` still returns it. The key does not have to hold a
+      value yet, which suits keys only some secrets hold. Keys are matched case-insensitively. Fails with
+        description: The length of `key` in bytes. `key` must be valid UTF-8, need not be null-terminated, and may be NULL only when this is 0.
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
+      Destroys the secret, releasing its resources. Values and views retrieved from it must not be used afterwards,
+      Null-safe: passing a null pointer or null handle is a no-op. The handle is set to null on return to prevent
+      double-destruction. Must only be called on an owned secret, never on the borrowed ones of a create callback.
